---
title: "Backends"
---


For each backend: the extra that installs it, its capability tier and flags,
the locator fields it reads (from `tether add` options / `--set` / `Repo.add`),
its `[backends.<kind>]` config in `tether.toml`, what it records as state, how
pins and forks map onto the system, the handle `open` returns, and what
`diff --content` reports. Credentials are never stored in manifests.

Common conventions:

- `branch` in a locator is the *base* ref (default `main`). With
  `--write fork`, `tether new` creates
  `tether.ws.<dataset8>.<ws8>.<key-slug>-<key6>` from the pin; with
  `--write track`, the working ref is the base branch itself.
- Pins are named `tether.<pin_id>` in the target system, where `pin_id` is
  `<dataset8>.<hash16>`: the dataset's id, then a content address of kind +
  identity + state. Backends treat the id as opaque; the engine keeps `gc`
  inside its own dataset's namespace.
- `identity` is the subset of the locator that names the system; two objects
  of one dataset with the same identity and state share one pin.
- `at` in a locator detaches the base at a native state (`tether add --at` /
  `--pick`); `tether log` lists what each system accepts:

| Kind | `at` accepts | `log` lists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icechunk` | snapshot id, tag, branch | `Repository.ancestry` from the ref: id, `written_at`, message |
| `lance` | version number (on the base branch) or tag | `versions()` of the branch, newest first, tags on each |
| `iceberg` | snapshot id or ref name | snapshot ancestry with operation and record counts |
| `delta` | version number | transaction log with operation and metrics |
| `ducklake` | snapshot id | `ducklake_snapshots` with each snapshot's changes |
| `lakefs` | commit id or tag | the ref's commit log |
| `dolt` | commit hash, tag, or branch (`HASHOF`) | `DOLT_LOG(ref)` |
| `git` | any commit-ish (alias of `ref`) | `git log` with decorations |
| `neon`, `file` | not supported | -- |

| Kind | Extra | Tier | Flags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | -- (local) / `objectstore` | Observed; Addressable for a versioned object | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `DIFF` |
| `icechunk` | `icechunk` | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE` |
| `neon` | `neon` | Forkable | `NEEDS_QUIESCENCE`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `BRANCH_IS_STORAGE` |
| `git` | -- | Forkable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE` |
| `iceberg` | `iceberg` | Forkable | `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE` |
| `delta` | `delta` | Addressable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF` |
| `lance` | `lance` | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF` |
| `lakefs` | `lakefs` | Forkable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE` |
| `ducklake` | `ducklake` | Addressable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF` |
| `dolt` | `dolt` | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE` |
| `memory` | -- | Forkable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE` (tests only) |

`PROMOTE` means `tether promote` can fast-forward the base branch to a fork
(Icechunk `reset_branch`, Iceberg `set-snapshot-ref`, git `merge --ff-only`,
lakeFS / Dolt merges); `MERGE` means it can three-way merge a diverged fork
(git `merge`, lakeFS `merge_into`, `DOLT_MERGE`). Lance cannot move a branch
head yet and Neon cannot promote a child branch, so both are refused with
instructions.

`--pin record` removes `PIN` from any of these: the state is recorded without a
native ref and `new` forks from it directly (Icechunk snapshot id, Lance
`(branch, version)`, Iceberg snapshot id, lakeFS/Dolt/git commit, Neon LSN on
the branch it was read from) for as long as the system still has that state.

## `file` -- local paths and object stores

Plain artifacts: a local file or directory, or an object / prefix in S3
(`s3://`), GCS (`gs://`), or Azure Blob (`az://`, `abfs://`), through
[obstore](https://developmentseed.org/obstore/).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional; `path` accepted). A trailing `/` (or empty key) means a prefix. `region` overrides the store region. |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `obstore.store.from_url` (region, endpoint, account name -- non-secret options). Credentials come from the environment / instance metadata. |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | local file: `type=file, size, mtime_ns`; local dir: `type=dir, count, size, digest`; remote object: `type=object, size, etag[, version_id]`; prefix: `type=prefix, count, size, digest` (one paged `LIST`, etag+size per key) |
| Tier | Observed by default. `--file versioned` on a single object makes it Addressable via `version_id` (S3 version id / GCS generation / Azure version id; requires versioning on the bucket/container). Prefixes are always Observed. |
| Pin / fork | none |
| Handle | `FileHandle(uri, version_id)` -- always read-only |
| Listing | directories and prefixes hand the engine a per-file JSONL listing (`{"p": path, "k": token, "s": size}`) that is stored under `.tether/listings/` |
| Diff | `files`: per-path added/removed/modified with size deltas from two stored listings; falls back to a count/size summary when a listing is missing; single objects report changed size/etag/mtime/version |
| Notes | `--file immutable` (default) turns any drift into an `ImmutableObjectModified` error at `status`. Local walks use `os.scandir`; symlinked directories are not followed. |

## `icechunk` -- Icechunk repositories

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (local path or `s3://bucket/prefix`), `branch` (default `main`), `region` (S3) |
| Config | none (S3 credentials from the environment) |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `snapshot_id` of the branch head |
| Pin | `create_tag("tether.<id>", snapshot_id)`; tags are immutable and exempt from expiry |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, snapshot_id)` off the tag (`reset_branch` if it exists) |
| Handle | `IcechunkHandle(repository, session, branch, tag, snapshot_id)`; `session` is writable for a branch, read-only for a tag/snapshot |
| Diff | `nodes`: `Repository.diff(from, to)` -- new/deleted groups and arrays, updated metadata, updated chunk counts per array, moves |

## `neon` -- Neon Postgres

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `project_id` (required), `branch` (default `main`), `database`, `role` (used for connection URIs) |
| Config | `api_key_env` (default `NEON_API_KEY`), `api_url` (default Neon API v2) |
| Identity | `{project_id, branch, database, role}` |
| State | `lsn`, `next_xid`, `branch` (probed over SQL on the working or source branch). `lsn` is volatile -- it advances on checkpoints -- so only `next_xid` and `branch` count as content; `branch` names the timeline the LSN belongs to |
| Pin | a protected child branch `tether.<id>` of the state's `branch` at `parent_lsn` (so a fork's pin hangs off the fork, not `main`); `RETENTION_BOUND` by the project's history retention |
| Fork | a child branch of the pin. Re-forking an existing working branch restores it onto the source (Neon branch restore, always -- a branch's `parent_id` says where it was created, not where its head is). Once a pin has been taken on the working branch that pin is its child and Neon will not restore it in place, so the fork lands on a sibling (`<name>.2`, `.3`, ...) and the old branch stays as the pins' parent; the engine records the returned name. `open` writable creates a `read_write` endpoint lazily; time-travel reads (`open` at a recorded state) ensure a `read_only` one |
| Quiescence | `commit` refuses while `pg_stat_activity` shows active writers (`--force` skips) |
| Handle | `NeonHandle(url, branch)` -- a Postgres connection URL |
| Diff | not supported (no native primitive) |
| Notes | pins are branches, so a working branch cannot be deleted while its pins exist; `gc` only drops leaf pins. Branches *are* the storage (`BRANCH_IS_STORAGE`): `gc --prune-workspaces` never deletes a Neon working branch without `--force-prune`. Neon cannot merge a child back into `main` -- use `--write track` for production. `protected` requires a paid plan. Fingerprinting may wake a suspended compute; use `--no-snapshot` when that matters. |

## `git` -- git and jj repositories

Pin the *code* (or any git-tracked data) that produced a dataset. Colocated
jj repositories work through their `.git`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `path` (local checkout; the positional locator works too: `tether add code --kind git ../code`), `ref` (default `HEAD`), `remote` (push pins there), `allow_dirty` (pin despite uncommitted changes) |
| Config | `git_path`, `jj_path` |
| Identity | `{path}` (resolved absolute) |
| State | `sha`; `dirty` (only meaningful -- and only computed -- for the checked-out ref); `change_id` when jj is available, volatile so the same sha pins identically with or without jj |
| Pin | lightweight tag `tether.<id>` at the sha (pushed to `remote` if set) |
| Fork | branch `name` at the tag's sha (`branch -f` if it exists) |
| Handle | `GitHandle(path, sha, worktree)` |
| Diff | `files`: `git diff --name-status -M` with `--numstat` line counts (`+a -d`) |
| Notes | remote-only (url) repositories are not supported yet. |

## `iceberg` -- Apache Iceberg tables (pyiceberg)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `identifier` (`ns.table`; `table` accepted), `branch` (default `main`), `catalog_name` (default `default`), `catalog` (dict of pyiceberg catalog properties, or set once in config) |
| Config | `catalog = {...}` pyiceberg properties (`type`, `uri`, `warehouse`, ...) |
| Identity | `{identifier, branch, catalog_name}` |
| State | `snapshot_id` (nothing else: `metadata_location` changes on every table commit on any branch) |
| Pin | `--pin native` (default): tag `tether.<id>`; `--pin record`: no native ref, the snapshot id alone (drops `PIN`; recoverable only within snapshot retention -- for S3 Tables and other catalogs where user refs disable maintenance) |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, snapshot_id)`; re-forking an existing name re-points it (a `set-snapshot-ref` update) |
| Handle | `IcebergHandle(table, ref, snapshot_id)` |
| Diff | `snapshots`: one entry per snapshot on `b`'s ancestry back to `a`, from snapshot summaries (`append: +5 rows, +1 files`); when `a` is not an ancestor, `total-*` counters are compared instead |

## `delta` -- Delta Lake tables (delta-rs)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional), `region` (sets `AWS_REGION`) |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `DeltaTable` (non-secret) |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `version`, `table_id` (metadata id -- a recreated table verifies as drifted) |
| Pin / fork | none: Delta has no tags or branches. Versions stay readable until `VACUUM` (7-day default) / log retention (30 days). |
| Handle | `DeltaHandle(uri, version, table)` -- read-only `DeltaTable` at the version |
| Diff | `commits`: one entry per transaction-log commit in `(a, b]` with its operation and metrics (`WRITE: +2 rows, +1 files`) |

## `lance` -- Lance datasets

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional), `branch` (default `main`) |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `lance.dataset` |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `branch`, `version` (Lance version numbers are branch-scoped) |
| Pin | `tags.create("tether.<id>", (branch, version))`; tagged versions are exempt from `cleanup_old_versions()` |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, tag)`. Lance refuses to delete a branch a tag references, so a pinned working branch outlives its workspace and a re-fork under the same name picks `name.2`, `name.3`, ... |
| Handle | `LanceHandle(uri, dataset, version, branch, tag)`; append with `lance.write_dataset(table, handle.dataset, mode="append")` |
| Diff | `fragments`: fragment ids added/removed, deletion-file changes, columns added/removed, from the two manifests |
| Notes | an untouched fork reports its parent's `(branch, version)`, so a no-op commit after `tether new` is a no-op. |

## `lakefs` -- lakeFS repositories

*Experimental*: tested against a fake (lakeFS, Dolt) or a local catalog (DuckLake), not against a live deployment; outside the core stack.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `repository` (required; `--repository`), `branch` (default `main`), `prefix` (scopes the handle URI and the diff; pins are repository-wide) |
| Config | keyword arguments for `lakefs.Client` (e.g. `host`); by default the SDK reads `LAKECTL_*` / `~/.lakectl.yaml` |
| Identity | `{repository}` |
| State | `commit_id` of the branch head, plus `dirty = true` when the staging area has uncommitted changes (refused at pin time) |
| Pin | tag `tether.<id>` at the commit |
| Fork | branch `name` from the tag (recreated if it exists at another commit) |
| Handle | `LakeFSHandle(uri, repository, ref, commit_id, prefix)` with `uri = lakefs://repo/ref/prefix/` (accepted by lakefs-spec, the S3 gateway, `lakectl`) |
| Diff | `objects`: server-side `Reference.diff` between the commits, scoped to `prefix`, with sizes |

## `ducklake` -- DuckLake catalogs (DuckDB)

*Experimental*: tested against a fake (lakeFS, Dolt) or a local catalog (DuckLake), not against a live deployment; outside the core stack.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `metadata` (positional `uri` accepted; the `ducklake:` prefix is added if missing, e.g. `ducklake:postgres:dbname=lake`), `data_path`, `table` (scopes the handle only -- snapshots are catalog-wide) |
| Config | `init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET ...", ...]` run on every fresh connection (put credentials here or in the environment, not in the locator) |
| Identity | `{metadata[, data_path]}` |
| State | `snapshot_id`, `snapshot_time_us` (epoch microseconds; a recreated catalog verifies as drifted) |
| Pin / fork | none: DuckLake has no tags or branches. `ducklake_expire_snapshots` bounds how long a snapshot stays readable. |
| Handle | `DuckLakeHandle(metadata, alias, connection, snapshot_id, attach_sql, data_path, table)`: a DuckDB connection with the catalog attached read-only (at `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` for a recorded state); `table_ref()` gives `alias.table`; `close()` / `with handle:` detaches |
| Diff | `tables`: per-table created/dropped/altered/inserted/deleted from the snapshots' `changes` maps, with row counts from `ducklake_table_changes` for tables that still exist |
| Notes | a DuckDB-file metadata catalog can be attached only once per process: operations attach/detach per call (serialized per catalog), and an open handle or your own writer connection in the same process blocks `status`. Postgres/SQLite/MySQL catalogs have no such limit. |

## `dolt` -- Dolt databases (MySQL protocol)

*Experimental*: tested against a fake (lakeFS, Dolt) or a local catalog (DuckLake), not against a live deployment; outside the core stack.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default 3306), `database` (required), `branch` (default `main`), `user`; or `url = mysql://user@host:port/database` |
| Config | `password_env` (default `DOLT_PASSWORD`), `user_env` (default `DOLT_USER`, used when the locator has no `user`) |
| Identity | `{host, port, database}` |
| State | `commit` (branch head hash), plus `dirty = true` when `dolt_branches.dirty` reports uncommitted working-set changes (refused at pin time) |
| Pin | `CALL DOLT_TAG('tether.<id>', commit)` |
| Fork | `CALL DOLT_BRANCH(name, tag)` (recreated with `-D` if it exists at another commit) |
| Handle | `DoltHandle(url, database, ref, commit)`: a revision-database URL `mysql://user@host:port/db/<branch|tag|hash>` (tags and hashes are read-only in Dolt); `database_ref` is `db/ref` for `USE` |
| Diff | `tables`: `dolt_diff_summary` (added/dropped/modified/renamed tables, schema changes) with `dolt_diff_stat` row counts |
| Notes | talks to `dolt sql-server` / Hosted Dolt via PyMySQL; the SQL surface sits behind the `DoltClient` protocol (`tether.backends.dolt`) so other transports can be substituted. |

## `memory` -- in-process reference backend

The executable specification of the protocol, used by the conformance suite and
the engine tests. Locator `{system, branch}`; state `snapshot_id`; tags and
branches in a process-global `MemoryStore` (`tether.backends.memory.default_store()`).
`MemoryHandle.read()` / `.write(payload)` operate on the current ref; `diff`
reports changed payload keys.
